title: sdk(python): add example for enabling quantization profile per route + verifying application
author: Ibrahim Khan
release_notes: Python SDK examples now include route-level quantization profile enablement (opt-in) and a verification pattern using debug resolution metadata.
description: Context: The Quantization Profile Library is opt-in and enabled at the route level via `quantization_profile_ref`. We’ve had repeated questions from design partners on (a) what the Python SDK call should look like for setting the route config and (b) how to confirm the profile actually applied (vs. policy fallback to baseline). This PR updates the Python SDK examples/snippets to show a full end-to-end flow: create/update a route with `quantization_profile_ref`, send a request through that route, and verify resolution by enabling debug metadata and checking the resolved `quant_profile_id`/outcome. What’s included: (1) New example: `examples/routes/enable_quantization_profile.py` showing `routes.update(...)` with `quantization_profile_ref="qpl:<model_id>:recommended"` and basic guardrails (try/except for incompatibility). (2) Added snippet to README + docs section clarifying semantics: `"default"` preserves baseline behavior; `"qpl:*"` is opt-in and may fallback if incompatible. (3) Verification guidance: enable debug resolution metadata and check `response.debug.route_resolution.quantization` fields (applied/fallback/disabled) plus the `quant_profile_id` when present. (4) Minor SDK typing/docstring updates in the `RouteUpdate` model to cross-link the feature and error behavior. Notes: This does not change any API surface area; it only updates examples + documentation to match control-plane behavior and the current debug payload shape from `redwood` PRs in the main repo. Follow-ups: once Console changelog + audit events are fully GA, we can add a docs link for “who changed what” and recommend correlating via request_id + audit logs.

snippet:
Example (new):

route = client.routes.update(
    route_id="rt_123",
    model="llama-3.1-70b-instruct",
    quantization_profile_ref="qpl:llama-3.1-70b-instruct:recommended",
)

resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    route_id=route.id,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize: ..."}],
    max_tokens=128,
    request_options={"include_debug": True},
)

q = getattr(resp, "debug", None)
if q and q.get("route_resolution"):
    quant = q["route_resolution"].get("quantization")
    # quant = {"outcome": "applied"|"fallback"|"disabled", "quant_profile_id": "qp_...", "reason": "..."}
    print("quant outcome:", quant)

review_conversation: Monica Patel: The example is great, but please avoid implying we’ll always return a quant_profile_id. When we fallback or when debug is off, it won’t be present. Can you update the snippet to show conditional checks and mention `include_debug` explicitly? Ibrahim Khan (author): Updated example to guard on debug presence and to print outcome + reason when fallback occurs. Also added a short note that without debug metadata you should rely on platform dashboards/audit logs for confirmation. Chloe Martin: The error handling text should match what the control plane returns for incompatibility. We’re using `incompatible_quantization_profile` with a remediation message (e.g., unsupported GPU class / max context). Can you update the docs copy to reflect that and not mention HTTP 409 specifically? Ibrahim Khan: Adjusted wording to avoid hardcoding status codes; example catches `RedwoodAPIError` and prints `e.code` + `e.message`. Alex Martinez: Please add a short callout in README: default behavior unchanged when field is unset or set to `default`, and this is opt-in per route (not tenant-global). Ibrahim Khan: Added callout under Routes -> Advanced configuration, plus link to the public docs PR for quantization profiles. Monica Patel: Approved after last pass. Chloe Martin: Approved.
